summary: This edition provides 76 complete documentation guides and 51 additional screened leads. 27 earlier screened entries received full guides. New and updated records carry their own dated evidence checks. Creative workflows include optical score recognition, camera-tracked shadow figures, editable voice-and-caption handoffs, subject mattes and depth layers, and editable local image masks. A current AutoShade guide covers material changes in the v1.18 line following the earlier v1.15 review. Software licensing is reviewed independently of model terms, any paid service or required proprietary host. NLLB translation and a browser background-removal route use separate noncommercial model grants. No discovered app was installed or run. The frozen plan covered 110 fields with 1222/1222 repository queries attempted. 1182 completed successfully, 8 were partial, and 32 failed. 227 were bounded. All 29 configured model tasks were attempted. 0 model tasks failed. The collection retained explicit warnings and limits. Metadata screening indexed all 2,543 saved repository pages, spanning 81,587 numeric identities. The complete retained backlog was consulted alongside today's metadata, including earlier pilot candidates. It currently has 113,692 raw records and 1,118 previously screened pending guides. A metadata signal does not establish software eligibility. Unreviewed and excluded candidates remain in private research records. Upstream credential-shaped metadata and signed media queries were redacted before sealing, with original hashes and redaction provenance retained locally. Live primary research beyond GitHub covered all observed fields and the configured ecosystems. The notes identify limits such as access and rate restrictions, failed fetches and bounded discovery pages. The counts represent the documented searches and available pages. The first aggregate pilot repository-tree index was reconstructed from the original saved response bodies; exact initial request timestamps for that aggregate were not recovered. Model-task responses with no rows: text2text-generation. Current cited reviews changed 2 prior labels. Vidyom moved from Quality unverified to Experimental. LiveKit Lite Avatar moved from Quality unverified to Experimental. The separate watchlist and evidence enrichment recorded 59 individual watchlist failures and 3 evidence failures. Source failures are retained as gaps.

ecosystem_checks.finding: Live repository topics and file APIs were researched. GridFab’s source tree, package configuration and full AGPL grant are available from the canonical GitLab repository. Its PyPI release and pre-alpha status support a scoped editor guide. The first guessed license filename returned 404; the actual LICENSE.md was recovered. OpenSlides returned an access error. These are bounded source checks.

The default-branch API, repository trees and complete grants yielded current evidence for Imaginer and Raspberry Pi 5 Diffusion. Imaginer’s initial main-branch paths were wrong. The repository specifies master and COPYING. Multiple Codeberg topic search APIs returned 429; current site/file visibility did not clear the incomplete discovery coverage.

Checked live project search pages for diffusion, whisper, creative work, captions and OSC, and revalidated the diffuser Cargo manifest and complete license. The local-path dependency is a setup limit for that existing entry. The breadth and installation of other tools were not established from these pages.

Reviewed live Python, JavaScript and Rust registry metadata, including GridFab’s Python/Tk release and the score-reader and MediaPipe components. Some guessed package names returned 404. Listings show component/version context without verifying complete source licenses or results.

Current Interstice and Krita pages give plugin integration context. The SpriteLoom docs separate its original Aseprite route and the MLX or agent adapters. A proprietary creative host, optional model and add-on software keep separate terms and requirements.

Live primary research covers every observed field and includes project sites, registries, research abstracts and direct source pages. AutoShade’s current site and releases distinguish reverse fitting from optional image generation. Unavailable pages, JavaScript shells and bounded captures retain their stated gaps.

Duke’s learned robotic shadow article and FoleyForge and ATune papers supply current research context. The examined primary material did not establish reusable code grants for those exact research systems. eShadow provides a distinct released implementation, and its learned segmentation route is narrower than learning a puppeteer’s movements.

Reviewed cross-language sources on Mandarin interaction, Greek/Flutter puppetry, Chinese Jianpu score workflows and Vietnamese subtitle localization. Sunway and CUNY projects add a different shadow-performance context. Their documentation does not itself clear artwork and recording terms or prove release availability.
